title: Buying Gold on Akshaya Tritiya? 8 Things to Check Before You Pay
intro: On Akshaya Tritiya many families buy gold, believing it brings lasting prosperity. In the festival rush it is easy to overpay. These eight checks will help you buy wisely.

p: Gold jewellery sold in India must carry the BIS hallmark. Check the purity mark (916 for 22 carat) and the six-character HUID, which you can verify in the BIS Care app.
Gold prices change daily. Compare the rate at two or three shops with a reliable online rate before you decide.
The price of jewellery includes making charges and sometimes wastage. These depend on the design, so ask for the percentage and negotiate.
The bill should list gold weight, stone weight, rate, making charges, GST and hallmark details separately. You will need it for resale and insurance.
Ask how much is deducted when you sell, and what the exchange policy is. Coins and bars have lower making charges, so they suit investment better.
Buy jewellery if you want to wear it. For pure investment, options such as gold ETFs and digital gold also exist, each with its own costs, rules and tax treatment. Use a regulated, trusted provider.
Festival offers on EMIs and gold loans can tempt you, but interest can wipe out any gain. Buy only what fits your budget.

sections.h: 8. Gold is not the only way
p: By tradition, charity and feeding the needy on this day are also said to give lasting merit. Even if you do not buy gold, you can still honour the day.

faq.q: Is it compulsory to buy gold on Akshaya Tritiya?
faq.a: No. It is a tradition and belief, not a rule. Charity and prayer are equally valued.
For jewellery, choose hallmarked pieces because the mark is your assurance of purity.

disclaimer: Note: this is general information, not financial or investment advice. Rules, limits and prices change, so check current details and speak to a qualified adviser before deciding.
